mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate signals tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to a decrease in S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a weakening labor market, which often precedes a downturn in economic activity and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 70% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between UNRATE increases and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real estate sales (HOUST) signals strong consumer demand, which is typically associated with positive economic growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 60% of instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between HOUST increases and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates a contraction in supply-side activity, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings are negatively impacted.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between INDPRO declines and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase significantly, it signals a strengthening labor market, which typically leads to increased consumer spending and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between PAYEMS increases and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real final sales (RSAFS) signals strong consumer demand, which is typically associated with positive economic growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 60% of instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between RSAFS increases and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and inflation (CPIAUCSL) both rise, it indicates a tightening monetary policy environment with potential for stagflation, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the joint effect of FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL increases on SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) rises and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) decline simultaneously, it signals a weakening labor market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises > 0.3pp and PAYEMS declines > 100k in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the joint effect of UNRATE increases and PAYEMS declines on SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
